sections.h2: What is different about selling inside Metro Nashville's single government?
sections.html:
Since 1963 the city and Davidson County have run as one Metro government, which puts valuation, billing and deed recording for a sale under one roof. Three small cities, Belle Meade, Ridgetop and Goodlettsville, collect their own city tax. Terrain matters too: the Cumberland River cuts through the Nashville Basin while the Highland Rim hills ring the west, so listings often mention slopes and retaining walls.

The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate for the Nashville-Davidson balance is 721,074 people, 4.6% above the April 2020 base. Only 52.4% of occupied units are lived in by the owner, so many sellers here are landlords, heirs or relocating workers. The table lists the Metro offices a seller is likely to call.

Metro officeIts role in a saleContact detail

sections.h2: What does Census data reveal about housing in Nashville?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts puts the typical owner-occupied home at $413,600 (2020 to 2024) and median gross rent at $1,586 a month. The balance counts 313,513 households averaging 2.13 people, and about four in five residents lived at the same address a year earlier.

  • Median household income: $77,371 in 2024 dollars
  • College graduates, 25 and older: 48.0%
  • Average commute: 24.7 minutes each way
  • Share of people in poverty: 14.1%

These are citywide averages. A downtown condo and a ranch house in Antioch can sit far from them, so look at recent sales on your own street before pricing. The figures come from Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: Why did Nashville tax bills jump after the 2025 reappraisal?
sections.html:
Values were mailed on April 18, 2025 and the median parcel rose 45%, with council district medians running from 38% to 54%. The Assessor points out that the state first cut the old rates to revenue-neutral ones, then Metro lifted them to $2.814 per $100 assessed in the Urban Services District and $2.782 in the General Services District. That is a 26% and a 39% rise over the certified rates. A value can be appealed; the rate cannot.

Residential property is assessed at 25% of appraised value. Take the Census median of $413,600: assessed value is about $103,400, and the Trustee's method yields roughly $2,909 in the Urban Services District or $2,876 elsewhere in the county. Informal reviews for 2025 closed on May 9 and formal appeals on June 27. Both dates are behind us, so call the Assessor at 615-862-6059 to learn how a future review works.

sections.h2: What will the Trustee's bill look like when I close?
sections.html:
The Trustee prints the annual statement for the parcel's owner of record, and it covers the whole calendar year. Your title company should divide it on the settlement sheet. Unpaid amounts follow the parcel, so confirm that the year is settled before you hand over keys.

  • Statements are sent the first week of October, with payment due on the first Monday of that month.
  • Payment is interest-free until February 28 or 29.
  • After that, 1.5% a month is added starting March 1.
  • A card payment adds 2.55% (minimum $2.00); an e-check adds $1.00.

Tennessee law does not require the Trustee to mail anything, so a bill that goes astray does not stop interest. A parcel left delinquent can be sold at a tax sale auction, and the former owner then has a year to redeem it.

sections.h2: Does Nashville offer property tax relief that a seller should mention?
sections.html:
Davidson County has a freeze for owners 65 and older, plus relief for low-income elderly or disabled homeowners and for disabled veterans. The Comptroller's 2026 table caps freeze income at $54,900 here. A veteran rated 100% disabled has no income test, and the relief applies to the first $175,000 of market value.

Tell the buyer's side early if you hold any of these, so the settlement figures match the bill actually due. The Trustee's office at 615-862-6330 can say which proofs of age, residence and income it wants.

sections.h2: What happens at the Register of Deeds on Deaderick Street?
sections.html:
Deeds are filed at 300 Deaderick Street, and the office also takes remote filings. State law sets a levy of 37 cents per $100 of price on the transfer. Documents must be originals with notarized signatures. Staff cannot draft a deed, and they cannot report liens, which is a job for a title company or attorney.

Indexes are open to the public, and online records are available by subscription. Ask the closer to record on the day you sign so the new deed is indexed quickly, and request a certified copy later if you need one for your files.

sections.h2: Does a short term rental permit stay with a Nashville house?
sections.html:
It does not. Metro Codes ties the permit to a named holder and one address, and any change of owner cancels it, including a move from a person into a trust or LLC. A buyer who wants nightly guests files from scratch.

  • A permit lapses 365 days after issue unless renewed.
  • The guest count tops out at twice the sleeping rooms plus four, never more than 12.
  • Renters must be 21 or older.
  • Three code violations can cost the holder the permit.

List the permit status in your offer paperwork so the buyer is not surprised. The Metro Codes operating rules spell out every condition.

sections.h2: What is the story behind Nashville's older neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Settlers built Fort Nashborough in 1779 beside the Cumberland. The town was incorporated in 1806, became the state's permanent capital in 1843, and a Metro charter joined it to the county in 1963. Nashville's public schools date to Hume School in 1855, and the unified Metro district now lists 160 schools.

Housing from many eras sits side by side. Sellers of older houses can pull the year built and living area from the Assessor's record and check them against the listing. Roof age, foundation movement and old wiring are the items buyers most often ask about, so price those in or fix them before showings.

sections.h2: What are the quickest ways to sell a Nashville house?
sections.html:
A listing reaches the most buyers but brings showings, appraisals and repair requests. A sale to a cash buyer who takes the house as-is trades some of that reach for speed, since closing waits on title work and not on a lender.

With any route, get the price in writing, confirm in the contract who pays recording tax, and let a title company prepare and record the deed. Clear liens, unpaid tax and any short term rental permit issues before the closing date.

faqs.q: Will I owe Davidson County tax if I sell in November?
faqs.a: Yes, for your share of the year. The October bill covers the whole calendar year and goes to the owner of record, so the closing statement should divide it between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Can a Nashville owner contest the tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The Assessor says only values can be appealed. The Mayor and Metro Council set the rate, which for 2025 was $2.814 in the Urban Services District and $2.782 in the General Services District.

faqs.q: How much does the state charge to record a Nashville deed?
faqs.a: The transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of price, and the state recording fee has a $10 minimum. The Register of Deeds has an online calculator for exact totals.

faqs.q: Can a buyer take over my short term rental permit?
faqs.a: No. Metro Codes bars assignment to another person, entity or address, and a change of ownership cancels the permit. The new owner must apply again.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Metro property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the Trustee's office, Suite 220 of the Howard Office Building, 700 President Ronald Reagan Way. Hours are weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Mail goes to PO Box 196358, Nashville, TN 37219-6358.
